verifications.claim: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA said in March it is targeting a launch window from 1 April to 6 April.'; R2: 'for a launch as soon as April 1.'; R4: 'Launch date NET April 1, 2026'; R5: 'Artemis II (NET April 1, 2026)'; R6: 'Wed, April 1 Launch window begins'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm NASA targeting April 1, 2026, as the start of the launch window or NET date for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day test flight around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'During the 10-day mission, the crew on Artemis II'; R3: 'send four astronauts on a roughly 10-day journey around the moon'; R4: 'Crew size 4... Mission duration 10 days (planned)... Crewed lunar flyby'; R5: 'planned to send four astronauts on a lunar flyby... 10-day mission'; R6: 'CREW SIZE | 4... MISSION DURATION | 10 days... Crewed Lunar Flyby'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state four astronauts, 10 days, lunar flyby/test flight around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket was returned to Launch Complex-39B in late March 2026 following delays.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis 2 emerges from the Vehicle Assembly Building March 20... arrived at Launch Complex 39B'; R3: 'SLS arrives at the pad... March 20, 2026... return to Launch Complex-39B... following delays... No launch until April.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS rollout/return to LC-39B on March 20, 2026 (late March), after delays and rollback.

verifications.claim: Daily two-hour launch windows are available between April 1 and April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA has multiple launch windows throughout April. The earliest is the 1st or 3rd... 4th-6th.'; R2: 'NASA has two-hour launch windows available daily between April 1 and 6'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly matches 'daily two-hour' windows April 1-6; R1 supports multiple windows in early April.

verifications.claim: The target launch date for the Artemis II mission is April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT (22:24 UTC).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first window opening at 6:24 p.m. Eastern on April 1.'; R4: 'NET April 1, 2026, 22:24:00 UTC (6:24 pm EDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely state the first window/target as April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT / 22:24 UTC.

verifications.claim: The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is Space Launch System (SLS) Rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R2: 'Space Launch System rocket'; R3: 'Artemis 2 Space Launch System rocket'; R4: 'Rocket Space Launch System'; R5: 'Space Launch System'; R6: 'SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Every source confirms SLS as the launch vehicle for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The launch location for the Artemis II mission is Kennedy Space Center, Launch Complex 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch pad at the Kennedy Space Centre in Florida'; R2: 'Launch Complex 39B'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center... Launch Complex-39B'; R4: 'Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly name Kennedy Space Center LC-39B as the launch site.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission type is crewed lunar flyby (no landing).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'send astronauts around the moon'; R3: 'around the moon'; R4: 'Crewed lunar flyby... no landing'; R5: 'lunar flyby'; R6: 'Crewed Lunar Flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as crewed lunar flyby/orbit around Moon, no landing.

verifications.claim: The crew for the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; R4: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen'; R6: 'Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Sources list exactly these four as the Artemis II crew.

verifications.claim: The duration of the Artemis II mission is 10 days, according to Space Center Houston.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Space Center Houston (R6) explicitly states 10 days duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first time in more than 50 years... last lunar landing in December 1972'; R4: 'first crewed deep-space and lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R5: 'first crewed mission around the Moon... since Apollo 17 in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission serves as a critical step before the Artemis III crewed lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'How successful the mission is will be critical in bringing NASA one step closer to landing astronauts on the moon, the goal of Artemis III'; R4: 'Artemis II will be followed by Artemis III... critical step'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states Artemis II critical for Artemis III lunar landing; R4 positions it as precursor.
